bullets.title: NVDA Mobilizes $500B AI Infrastructure SPV with Major Wall Street Firms
bullets.body: NVIDIA formally announced a $500B+ capital mobilization effort partnering with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to fund AI infrastructure customers. One skeptic framed it as the 'world's biggest circle jerk SPV,' noting the structure is a memo of understanding rather than binding agreement, while another highlighted that hyperscaler/NVDA purchase commitments now exceed $1T and grow by $350B/quarter. Jensen Huang separately framed GPU compute as a financeable infrastructure asset with cash flow and residual value—'the most important part' of the announcement beyond the headline figure.

bullets.title: Intel $20B Equity Raise Prices at ~$95/Share on $100B+ Demand
bullets.body: Intel upsized its share sale to $20B after drawing more than $100B in investor demand, pricing at roughly $95/share (a ~6.5% discount). Demand described as 'off the charts.' The fundraise and Intel's elevated 2027 capex guidance are being read as a signal of confidence in sustained AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: LITE Pre-Earnings: Revenue Approaching $1B Milestone; EML Shortage a Tailwind
bullets.body: Ahead of earnings, one poster summarized LITE's guidance as $960M-$1.01B—approaching the psychological $1B threshold—with EML supply falling 30%+ short of demand and unit growth exceeding 50% YoY. The author flagged new products expected to drive continued acceleration. Separately, one commenter noted LITE (along with COHR, AAOI, CIEN) is dominated by algorithmic trading, advising holders to hold rather than churn.

bullets.title: MU: Customer Roadmap Visibility Extends Beyond 2030; Memory Packaging Inflation Ahead
bullets.body: At a KeyBanc discussion, MU's Sumit Sadana cited 'deep engineering engagements with customers' and visibility into roadmaps beyond 2030, confirming strong demand momentum. UBS noted NVIDIA's decision to lower HBM specs for Vera Rubin Ultra boosts VR300 unit supply and raises 2027 HBM consumption to 61.5B Gb from 58.7B Gb. Separately, Korea's DRAM export unit prices rose in early August, and semiconductor packaging price hikes are outpacing foundry increases through H2 2026.

bullets.title: Michael Burry Adds PLTR Puts, Values Stock Under $1
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag Michael Burry is increasing PLTR put options and believes the stock is worth under $1—a 99%+ decline from current levels. Counterpoint: S&P 500 is up 90%+ since Burry's last major sell call, implying weak track record on macro timing.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler IG Credit Spreads Blow Out to 143bps Despite Stocks at ATH
bullets.body: IG Hyperscaler OAS spreads reached 143bps in August, up 43bps from May-June lows of ~90bps—an historically unprecedented combination alongside equities at all-time highs and VIX below 20. One credit analyst called this 'never seen before' and questioned whether 'AA' credits have ever blown out 40bps in 60 days with stocks at ATH. Meanwhile, 19 firms sold IG debt in a single session, the most since January.

bullets.title: 30-Year Treasury Yields Hit 19-Year High at 5.28%; France Bond at Post-GFC High
bullets.body: US 30-year yields touched 5.28%, a 19-year high, with bond traders and the market signaling inflation concern as the Fed holds rates at 3.50%-3.75% under Chair Warsh's data-dependent stance. France's 30-year yield simultaneously hit its highest level since the 2008 GFC. Cleveland Fed's Hammack said current rates aren't 'meaningfully restricting the economy' and expects 'some number' of future hikes.

bullets.title: CXMT 17nm DDR5 Yield Exceeds 90%; Products Available in Spot Market
bullets.body: According to Chinese media, CXMT's 17nm DDR5 yields have surpassed 90%, with large volumes appearing in South China's spot market. Products are available for procurement by brands based on pricing and specification. One commenter noted this follows 80% yield reported last year on the same node, suggesting rapid improvement.

bullets.title: TSMC: CPU Demand Emerging as Growth Driver; Capacity Sold Out at Every Node Through 2028
bullets.body: WSJ reports CPUs are becoming a new growth driver for TSMC beyond AI, while a separate podcast-format post stated TSMC capacity is fully sold out at every node with AI customer bookings locked through 2028. VisEra (TSMC's optical components affiliate) is also scaling into 800G pluggable transceivers and targeting next-gen 1.6T silicon photonics.

bullets.title: South Korean Semiconductor Exports Surge; DRAM +32% QoQ, NAND +70% QoQ
bullets.body: Preliminary South Korean semiconductor export data for August 1-11 showed DRAM at $4.62B (+4% MoM, +32% QoQ) and NAND at $780M (+54% MoM, +70% QoQ). SSD exports declined 33% MoM and 54% QoQ. Total exports rose 45.3% YoY for the period, consistent with memory demand strength noted across sell-side commentary.

bullets.title: MSFT Planning Major Maia 300 AI Chip Ramp; Targeting TSMC Capacity
bullets.body: Microsoft is planning a major production ramp of its next-gen Maia 300 AI accelerator—potentially unveiled as early as next month—with TSMC capacity talks underway. The goal is to lower cost per token and reduce dependency on external GPUs in Azure inference and training workloads.

bullets.title: HIMS Q2 Revenue Beats at $753M; Q3 Guide $880M-$900M, Raises Full-Year to $3.1B-$3.3B
bullets.body: HIMS & HERS Q2 revenue of $753M beat estimates of ~$700M, but EPS of -$0.37 significantly missed the -$0.05 consensus. Q3 revenue guidance of $880M-$900M and FY 2026 raised to $3.10B-$3.30B vs. prior $2.93B. Company is testing peptide ingredients including BPC-157 ahead of an FDA decision on compounding, with gross margins expected to remain below historical levels.

bullets.title: AMD: Bullish Options Flow and AI Infrastructure Partnership Expansion
bullets.body: Large bullish AMD options prints noted during the session with the poster flagging 'millions worth of bullish AMD prints' as semiconductor momentum picked up. Separately, AMD exercised an option to expand its existing data center compute deal with HUT. PLTR was also cited +37% on S&P inclusion and AMD revenue +50% as recent headline performance.

bullets.title: S&P 500 P/B Ratio at All-Time High; Hyperscaler Capex Doubles to $789B
bullets.body: The S&P 500 price-to-book ratio surpassed the dot-com bubble peak, hitting an all-time high. Hyperscaler capex expectations for 2026 exploded from $460B to $789B in six months (+72%), with Goldman's baseline AI capex growing from $765B in 2026 through 2031. S&P 500 earnings are now expected to grow 32% in 2026, more than double the 15% expected at the start of the year.

bullets.title: Optical Networking: FCC Action Creates Market Bifurcation; COHR, LITE, AAOI Stressed
bullets.body: Two separate FCC actions are reportedly being conflated, creating contradictory market moves: Chinese optical stocks fell on U.S. sanction rumors while U.S. optical stocks (COHR, LITE, AXTI, AAOI) also declined on fears the sanctions won't actually be imposed. One analyst flagged the need to 'stress test' FCC 26-50 implications carefully, noting CLSA is 'correctly reading' the July rule. The InP supply chain—NVDA→LITE→AXTI—is linked via an $87M deposit.

bullets.title: AAPL 20th Anniversary iPhone Redesign Confirmed; Glass-Centric V73 Moving Forward
bullets.body: Contrary to analyst reports of a cancellation, Apple is still moving forward with a glass-centric iPhone redesign for its 20th anniversary flagship. New Pro models are internally called 'V73.' Separately, Micron is cautioning customers against deviating from supply contract agreement (SCA) terms, implying supply allocation risk for non-compliant customers in the next shortage.

bullets.title: Arista at Risk if Broadcom's Co-Packaged Optics Strategy Wins
bullets.body: One analyst posed that if Broadcom integrates optical engines directly into switch silicon (CPO), Arista's hardware value-add erodes and it risks becoming 'a box assembler.' Arista's stated interest in XPO (external packaging optics) is framed as a competitive necessity against Broadcom's vertical integration strategy.

bullets.title: Wednesday CPI Print Now the Key Macro Catalyst; Core Seen +0.2%
bullets.body: Most forecasters see core CPI rounding down to 0.2% in July. A mild print would validate the disinflation thesis and reduce pressure on Fed policy, but overlapping shocks continue to erode confidence in the official forecast. Fed's Hammack separately stated inflation won't fall on its own and current rates aren't 'meaningfully restricting' the economy, signaling continued hawkishness.

bullets.title: Meta Launches $1B Fund for Communities Hosting AI Data Centers; Open-Sources Large Models
bullets.body: Meta announced a $1B 'Future Is For Everyone' fund to support U.S. cities hosting its AI data centers. Separately, one commenter expressed hope that Meta would open-source its 'watermelon pretrain' multi-trillion-parameter models, and Zuckerberg stated AI will create 'an abundance of jobs' in the future.

bullets.title: Alchip July Sales +181.8% YoY to Record NT$7.43B on Amazon Trainium3 Ramp
bullets.body: Custom ASIC designer Alchip reported July sales of NT$7.43B (new all-time high), up 181.8% YoY and more than doubling June's NT$3.57B. The surge is attributed to Amazon's Trainium3 AI chip going into mass production. This is a direct read-through for AMZN AI silicon buildout demand.
